provenance.paper_title: MAGNET: Towards Adaptive GUI Agents with Memory-Driven Knowledge Evolution

evidence.paraphrase: Stationary memory links diverse visual features to stable functional semantics.
Procedural memory captures stable task intents across changing GUI workflows.
During operation, MAGNET applies fixed-rule insertion or replacement to stationary visual-semantic memory; the memory state changes while the governing update policy remains fixed.
During operation, MAGNET applies merging or deduplication of overlapping entries to stationary visual-semantic memory; the memory state changes while the governing update policy remains fixed.
Visual-semantic and procedural associations are updated across interface changes. For MAGNET, this specifically supports relinking or reindexing of stored items of stationary visual-semantic memory.

Frequently accessed knowledge is prioritized while both memories are refined. For MAGNET, this specifically supports evidence-weighted revision of stored belief or confidence of stationary visual-semantic memory.

derived.hybrid_relation: Distinct operative representation paths are explicitly linked for downstream retrieval, reasoning, or control.

adjudication_notes: Strict-tier full-paper review (PDF p. 4): During inference, the operative memory component (stationary visual-semantic memory) changes through fixed-rule insertion or replacement, merging or deduplication of overlapping entries, relinking or reindexing of stored items, evidence-weighted revision of stored belief or confidence; the governing policy remains fixed, and any learning reported by the paper occurs before deployment. Training-time learning, when present, was not counted as T3.
